subject.title: [Feature]: Per-binding and per-agent permissionMode for ACP sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a public scoped ACP permission default, and should it be exposed as generic permissionProfile or ACPX-specific permissionMode/nonInteractivePermissions in bindings and agent runtime config?
rationale: This changes a security-sensitive configuration boundary for automatic file-write and shell approval, and the current code already has both global ACPX permissionMode and live ACP permissionProfile concepts that need one maintainer-approved contract.

options.title: Approve generic scoped permissionProfile
options.body: Add binding and agent runtime defaults using the existing generic permissionProfile/runtime option model, then map to backend-advertised ACP/ACPX keys with security docs and tests.

options.title: Approve ACPX-specific permissionMode
options.body: Expose permissionMode and nonInteractivePermissions directly on scoped config, accepting tighter coupling to ACPX semantics for a clearer operator path.

options.title: Keep global-only defaults
options.body: Decline scoped defaults and document that mixed-trust ACP agents require separate gateways or manual per-session /acp permissions updates.

recommendation.title: Approve generic scoped permissionProfile
recommendation.body: Add binding and agent runtime defaults using the existing generic permissionProfile/runtime option model, then map to backend-advertised ACP/ACPX keys with security docs and tests.
